# Plan: overnight SPE rounds 5 to 8 (unattended)

The project details were not given, so this plan takes the round 4 artifacts in `spe/` as the starting point. These are `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` and the "Proposed for round 5" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`.

## What I need from you before you leave

- **Approve this plan.** This approval covers every round tonight. I will not wait for plan mode approval again. Each prediction file will say "Claude, autonomous, under the overnight approval of 2026-10-21".
- **Check the three caps below.** I chose them myself because "as many as make sense" has no number. If you say nothing, I will use them.

## Caps (defaults I chose)

| Cap | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds | At most 4 more (r05 to r08) | 3 matching rounds in a row (r05 to r07) is the stop rule. One more round leaves room for one miss. |
| Spend per round | 1.5 times the measured r04 cost | It allows growth from one change per round. Trials that would go over the cap are skipped and logged. |
| Total spend overnight | 4 times the measured r04 cost | This equals 4 rounds at the r04 cost. I halt when the next round's estimate would go over it. |
| Clock | No new round starts after 06:00 local time | You will find a closed round in the morning, not one that is half done. |

## What I will never do tonight

- I will not push, open PRs, deploy, or send messages. Commits and tags stay local.
- I will not edit a saved prediction after any trial has run.
- I will not change a grader to make a prediction hit. A grader fix needs a failure ID. The log then shows the original number and the regraded number side by side.
- I will not make any band wider than its r04 band. A wider band would let the 3-match stop rule pass without the predictions being any better.
- I will not change a task and a grader in the same round. Each configuration changes one thing.

## One round, step by step

I repeat these steps for each round. The table uses r05 as the example. `NN` is the round number, and the script holds it in a single `ROUND` constant.

| Step | What I do | Files | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Specify | I save the transcript. For r05 it holds your message, word for word. For r06 and later it says there was no new prompt and points to the r05 transcript. I adopt or reject each "Proposed for round NN" row with a reason, and each one becomes a requirement row. Its source is a failure ID such as "r04 F9" or "default (autonomous)". I log every choice I make in your place as a default. | `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-rNN.md`, `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/spec/disagreements.md` | `SPE rNN specify` |
| 2. Predict | I start from the previous round's draft yaml with `same_as_last_round` filled in. I move a number only when an adopted row gives a reason. Every cell is a number with a band and a one-line Why. Each number names its grader check. | `spe/plans/rNN.md`, `spe/predictions/rNN.yaml` (headed `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`) | `SPE rNN predict: ...` before any harness work |
| 3. Harness | I write the Workflow script. Trials get a schema. Code checks run first, and judges handle only what code cannot check. Trials cannot read graders, answers, or predictions. | `spe/evals/harness/rNN-workflow.js` | `SPE rNN evaluate (harness)` |
| 4. Gates | The grader selftest must show the oracle passing and the empty and wrong answers failing. I regrade the previous round as a control, and it must reproduce the logged numbers. A dry run on 2 or 3 cells must finish cleanly. If any gate fails, the Workflow does not launch. | Gate output in the round folder | None |
| 5. Run | I launch the Workflow with the spend cap set. Split cells get extra trials up to the cap. I wait for the completion notice and start nothing new before it arrives. I scan the transcripts and void any trial that peeked. The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic. | Results in `spe/evals/` | `SPE rNN evaluate (results): <headline>` |
| 6. Learn | I add the prediction log table, with a "Which Why broke" note for each miss. I say plainly when the naive guess was closer than the predictions. I add new F-numbered failures, starting from the highest F number already in the file. I write the "Proposed for round NN+1" table, the next draft yaml, and the README paragraph with the rerun command. | `spe/prediction-log.md`, `spe/failures.md`, `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/predictions/rNN-draft.yaml`, `spe/README.md` | `SPE rNN learn: ...`, tag `spe-rNN` |

## Round 5 content

- **Specify:** The rows come from the "Proposed for round 5" table that round 4 wrote. I adopt the proposals that fix a logged failure. I reject any proposal that needs a new paid resource or a scope change, and I log it in `disagreements.md` as waiting for you.
- **Predict:** All numbers start equal to the r04 measured values in `r04-draft.yaml`, with the r04 bands. The only numbers that move are the ones on the configuration that carries the adopted change. Each moved number gets a stated reason.
- **Evaluate:** I use the same Workflow arguments as r04, with the r05 cap. I log an unmeasured cost estimate in the plan before launch.

## How I choose the next round

- If every configuration passed everything, the next round gets harder tasks or a stricter grader. It does not get both.
- If a round missed, the next round changes the one assumption named under "Which Why broke".
- I count a round as a "match" when at least 90% of cells hit and the primary metric hits. I picked this definition as a default and logged it.

## When I stop

**Stop and report:** I stop after 3 matching rounds in a row, or when the round cap, the total spend cap, or the clock cap is reached.

**Halt at once and report:** I halt if a spend cap would be crossed, an answer key leaks to trials, or a gate shows a broken grader. I also halt when a failure needs a choice only you can make. Examples are scope changes, new paid resources, and dropping a requirement that came from your own words.

## What you will see in the morning

The report comes in chat, and `spe/README.md` will hold the same summary. It has these parts:

1. A headline for each round, r05 onward.
2. A prediction accuracy trend with hit rate per round and whether the naive guess was closer.
3. New failure IDs and which ones are still open.
4. Open decisions from `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
5. Total spend against the caps, and the list of local commits and tags. Nothing was pushed.
